title: Scalable credit caps and gradual-degradation reconciler
author: Marta Ruiz
description: Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets observed sudden SLA regressions under sustained burst patterns where per-tenant credit pools were exhausted and the cluster dropped from optimal throughput to hard-throttle mode. This PR introduces a scalable credit-capping controller and a gradual-degradation reconciler that: 1) enforces per-tenant soft caps and dynamic overflow gates, 2) applies a time-decayed degradation path (graceful throttling) instead of abrupt eviction, and 3) emits high-resolution tenant utilization quantiles for downstream billing and SLO reports. Changes include a controller that reconciles tenant credit state in bounded batches, a token gate that performs probabilistic admission when credits are low, and an exporter that produces p50/p90/p99 histograms per tenant window. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1217) [x] unit tests for reconciliation logic [x] e2e smoke tests against small Dedicated cluster [x] observability hooks and dashboards [x] rollout plan and feature flag gating Deployment notes: rollout behind feature flag dedicated.credit_reconciler=true; start with pilot tenants, monitor tenant_quantiles.dashboard, and enable global rollout after 48h of stable signals. Rollback: flip feature flag off; reconciler runs idempotently and previous ledger state is preserved. Related: complements ENG-1398 (headroom hedging) and fixes SUP-4421 customer incident summary. No API changes to public Redwood API surface. This description is single-line for PR export consistency.
